title: Privilege Orchestrator: unified policy evaluator, adaptive enforcement, and admin gateway adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a single 'Privilege Orchestrator' service that performs RBAC v2 policy evaluation and exposes enforcement adapters for the API gateway, runtime interceptors, and the admin console. This ticket covers the evaluator core, policy compiler, short-lived cache strategy, audit-forwarding hooks, and the admin gateway adapter that enforces scoped admin actions and records detailed audit events.

Scope:
- Policy semantics: support role->permission mappings, attribute-based conditions (user attributes, resource labels, request context), temporal constraints (start/end TTL), and allow-list/deny-list overrides for emergency breakglass.
- Evaluator core: fast in-memory rule index, hot-path C API (FFI) for runtime attach, deterministic decision output (allow/deny/explain metadata). Target median eval latency < 4ms at 50k req/s with 100ms p99 budget for full explain.
- Caching: multi-level cache (local LRU per node + shardable shared cache in Dedicated) with configurable TTL and invalidation hooks from policy updates.
- Audit & observability: each decision emits structured audit event (actor, resource, action, decision, policy_id, explain, trace_id). Provide an audit-forwarder that can stream to existing logging pipeline (Kafka/Cloud Logging/Splunk).
- Enforcement adapters: API gateway plugin, runtime interceptor library (C#/Go/Rust shim), and admin-console adapter that filters UI actions and dims unavailable controls. The admin adapter must also support scoped admin tokens (scoped to projects or route prefixes) and require re-authn for destructive actions.
- SSO/SAML mapping: extend identity mapping to accept SAML group attributes and map to roles, including support for attribute transforms and fallback mapping when groups are missing.
- Rollout & safety: canary rollout strategy, automatic fallback to legacy authorizer on error, and a 'read-only audit' mode to validate policy coverage before blocking traffic.

Design decisions made so far:
- Use a compact flattened policy DSL (inspired by attribute-rule tables) and compile into a numeric instruction stream to reduce eval overhead; this avoids embedding a full Rego-like engine which adds complexity and memory pressure.
- Emit a single canonical audit JSON per request that includes both the raw decision and the explain path (policy ids + matched clauses). This ensures downstream SIEMs can reconstruct incidents without sampling.
- Integrate SAML group mapping into the identity ingestion path rather than the evaluator; evaluator receives normalized 'principal.roles' and 'principal.attrs' fields. This simplifies evaluator code and keeps identity transforms auditable.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end request path: API request authenticated -> evaluator returns decision within SLO -> enforcement adapter enforces and audit event is produced and visible in staging Logs.
2) Policy update path: changing a policy in admin console invalidates caches within 5s in Dedicated and 30s in Hosted; no stale-allow windows longer than configured TTL.
3) Admin console: UI respects evaluator decisions (controls hidden/disabled) and scoped admin tokens prevent cross-project destructive actions in test harness.
4) Security review: completed and documented with mitigation checklist for breakglass, token rotation, and secrets storage.

Success metrics:
- Decision latency median < 4ms, 99th < 20ms in staging baseline.
- Audit coverage >= 99% of enforced decisions.
- No user-facing regressions for 2 weeks post canary.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/13456789/Privilege+Orchestrator+Design
- Prototype PR (eval core): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876
- Admin gateway mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-admin-gateway-mockups
- Load test results (prototype): https://internal-dashboard.redwood.com/runs/priv-orch-2026-02

Notes on uniqueness: this ticket focuses on a compact compiled evaluator and a UI-aware enforcement adapter for admin controls (versus prior work that targeted sidecars or generic proxies). It also mandates a canonical audit JSON and SAML->role transform rules that are auditable and reversible.
